ai.claude: The result is narrower than the headline: it fixed one clear defect in one small model and failed where no such defect existed. The more useful near-term use is the one the authors mention last, checking models for hidden problems, which is an audit tool, not a takeoff.
ai.fact: MIT researchers report that OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra improved a small Alibaba Qwen model by editing 0.016% of its weights directly, cutting its habit of repeating itself and lifting its maths score from 7.9% to 48.1% without any retraining. The same method barely moved Google's small Gemma 3, which had no single obvious flaw to fix.

opinion.text: once models can alter and improve weights, AI starts speeding up its own progress.

austrian.claude: The argument is a useful warning for cantons and countries that compete only on rates. The counterpoint is that Zug also kept its edge because rates stayed low for decades; capital built up partly because it was not taxed away, so the tax rate is part of the seed, not only the harvest.
austrian.fact: Zug's income was already about 10% above the Swiss average by 1910, long before its tax cuts, Scholarium notes, so the later low rates met banks, rail links, skilled workers and firms that were already there.

opinion.text: copying Zug's tax rate does not copy decades of capital; without predictable administration, respect for property and quick decisions, low taxes will not make a second Zug.

mainstream.claude: After France, Belgium is the second euro member this autumn where a coalition breaks over the same question. Markets let it pass while the ECB stands behind them; Switzerland's debt brake looks like the boring answer that works.
mainstream.fact: Belgium's King Philippe has put off deciding whether to accept Prime Minister Bart De Wever's resignation after weekend budget talks broke down over a gap of about $11 billion, AP reports. The five-party coalition of nationalists, liberals and social democrats split over whether to cut social spending or raise taxes on the wealthy, with public debt above 108% of GDP and Belgian borrowing costs at 15-year highs.

opinion.text: with debt that high and yields rising, doing nothing is the most expensive option.

top.claude: The likely result is a president with less room at home and more appetite abroad, where Congress has little grip. That makes Iran, Ukraine and trade the places to watch tomorrow, not only the seat count. Results from the West Coast arrive overnight Zurich time.
top.fact: Voters cast ballots on Tuesday in US midterm elections dominated by the cost of living, with final polls putting Democrats in position to take at least one chamber of Congress and Trump's approval near record lows, Semafor reports. Forecasters expect the House to flip, while the Senate, which confirms judges and cabinet secretaries, is closer. Semafor's energy desk calls the vote a test of how much voters will punish the president for high petrol prices after the Iran war.

opinion.text: voters hoping Congress will fix affordability are going to be disappointed, since prices depend little on who holds the chambers.

top.fact: The United States struck targets on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, the latest in a series of limited strikes meant to keep the waterway open, as reported by Semafor and Arab News. Washington reportedly kept the strikes quiet to avoid signalling a return to full hostilities on the eve of the vote, while Vice President JD Vance said a deal could be close. Gulf exporters are finding other routes: Saudi Aramco's third-quarter net profit rose by more than a third on the year.

opinion.text: Vance launched the failed deal in June and has every reason to sound upbeat before an election that may punish his party for record fuel prices.

top.fact: Alphabet, Meta and Oracle have issued or are reported to plan new bonds while interest rates rise, and demand has surged for options and credit-default swaps that protect against an AI downturn, Semafor reports. Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum, which makes lasers for AI data centers, in a $115 billion all-stock deal, the company said. Anthropic's updated IPO filing shows nearly $17 billion of third-quarter revenue and a $567 million operating loss. Memory-chip prices have doubled in a year as Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron favour data-center buyers, Nikkei reports.

top.fact: The US said it will mediate talks between Ukraine and Russia next week, which International Intrigue reports will be held in Abu Dhabi, with parallel talks with Europe on security guarantees for Kyiv. Kyiv said an overnight Russian strike killed 29 people at an aid center and warned of a possible massive attack, while Russia said it downed almost 500 drones heading for Moscow. Latvia, which took over the UN Security Council presidency this month, called an emergency session on the strike.

top.claude: Washington frames it as routine eligibility rules, but the timing reads as pressure. Trade preferences are among the few levers the US still has in Africa, and each use makes them worth less.
top.fact: The United States will suspend South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act, which gives duty-free access to the US market, from 2027, Reuters and Semafor report. Relations with Pretoria have soured since Trump's false claim of a genocide against white South Africans, while Rwanda is accused of backing the M23 militia in eastern Congo, where US firms want to mine. South Africa could lose thousands of jobs in a country with one of the world's highest unemployment rates.

opinion.text: the move could push both countries closer to China.

top.fact: China will this month start controlling exports of construction equipment, in particular the large tunnel-boring machines used for transport infrastructure, Semafor reports, citing The New York Times. The curbs follow controls on solar-manufacturing equipment announced last month and limits on drone technology.

opinion.text: Beijing is doubling down on making Chinese factories indispensable even as other governments try to depend on them less.
